timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm a Catholic sister of the way of being Catholic called Roman Catholic.
Today, Catholic social teaching upholds as the very first principle as respect for the
dignity of life. And if we really absorb that, then we must be civil in our discourse
with one another. Recently, I've been very involved with the Muslim community in a variety
of ways. About a year and a half ago, I was on the stage as it worked with a very well-known
Muslim man and a Jewish man in the area. And there was about a hundred people that
were keen to listen to us, maybe a little less. And the tone of events became very, very
hostile and very violent for a while. So the Muslim man nodded to me and I got up because
I wasn't really sure how to handle this. And I got up in front of the group and I said,
what is common to all our religions is silence. And silence is we love, we say we love it
in our religious practice. So let's all now be silent for a minute. And everybody in
the group calmed down and were silent and the hostility subsided. None of this would
